you want deeply interactive game worlds

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players praise the incredible environmental interactivity and detail, though some experience initial performance issues.

claims.claim: The game features high levels of environmental interactivity, allowing players to interact with objects like bottles, doors, and drawers.

citations.review_text:
Long time Half-Life fan; I was never able to play the game at launch and only recently got a chance to play it all the way through on the Steam Frame. Despite having the story & ending spoiled for me shortly after it released, being able to experience it all first-hand after six years of waiting was still an incredible experience.

The environments, gameplay, voice acting, and huge levels of interactivity are what made Half-Life 2 special, and Alyx takes those elements and elevates them tenfold through VR. By far my favourite entry in the series now, very eager to see where Valve takes the franchise from here.
Holy peak i love the way we can interact with almost everything in the game🥹

Score: 10/10

Half-Life: Alyx is a virtual reality first-person shooter that places players in the role of Alyx Vance during humanity's occupation by the Combine. Designed exclusively for VR, it combines immersive storytelling, environmental interaction, exploration, and intense combat into one of the most polished virtual reality experiences ever created.

What it does well

✅ Unmatched VR Immersion

Every interaction feels natural, from opening drawers to reloading weapons by hand.
The game makes full use of motion controls to create a convincing sense of presence.

✅ Exceptional World Design

City 17 is packed with detail and atmosphere.
Every environment feels believable, lived-in, and carefully crafted.

✅ Engaging Combat

Encounters reward careful movement, resource management, and precision.
Enemies remain threatening throughout the campaign without becoming unfair.

✅ Excellent Puzzle Design

Environmental puzzles blend naturally into exploration.
Multi-tool hacking sequences add variety without interrupting the pacing.

✅ Outstanding Audio and Visuals

Lighting, animations, and environmental effects create a remarkable level of realism.
The sound design enhances every firefight and exploration sequence.
Weaknesses

❌ VR Hardware Required

A compatible VR headset is necessary, making the game inaccessible to players without one.

❌ Limited Weapon Variety

The arsenal is relatively small, though each weapon is highly refined and satisfying to use.

❌ Can Be Intense

Certain sections feature dark environments and frightening enemies that may be uncomfortable for some players.
Who will enjoy it?

You'll probably enjoy it if you like:

Story-driven adventures
Virtual reality gaming
Science-fiction settings
Exploration
Environmental puzzles
Atmospheric shooters
Standout Features
Full VR interaction
Immersive environmental storytelling
Physics-based gameplay
Detailed world design
Weapon upgrades
Memorable enemy encounters
Exceptional voice acting and sound design

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early players find combat demanding with rigid enemies, balancing mixed feelings on movement and challenge.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat as featuring heavy enemy health pools that require extensive headshot output, alongside static enemy AI and restrictive movement during fights.

citations.review_text:
HL: ALYX is [i]THE[/i] VR game

An immersive world, streamlined storytelling, and some genuine high tension moments that can only happen in VR. Valve fully embrace VR in game design and made it seem more natural and intuitive than any other VR experience I've had. The story is good, if you're a Half-Life fan it's great, mind-blowing even (no spoilers), but if you haven't played the previous games it stands on it's own just fine.

The blend of action, horror, and puzzle gameplay is just right. The 3-dimensional hacking/puzzles are great, though the end game ones can get a little frustrating. Throwing things in VR is always a little wonky but makes it more satisfying if you so land the perfect grenade. Combat overall is immersive and fun, though there were some times I swear i was being hit through walls or around corners, it's obviously hard to tell where your own hitbox ends, and the Combine all seem to have laser accuracy. My biggest complaint was enemy health pools, even standard soldiers take almost a full magazine of headshots. Your health doesn't last long and moving around during fights feels discouraged. Combat tends to devolve into repeatedly peaking one corner between enemy bursts to mag dump headshots, rinse and repeat. I would have liked if enemies had 1/3 the health but were three times as numerous, it would have felt more productive. If it was a normal 2D game the combat would be kinda boring, but the fact you're actually leaning in and out of cover and aiming just makes it click on a whole new level. 

My whole play-through was streamed to Steam Frame from a  Bazzite PC (make sure you select Proton version in compatibility setting as native Linux build is missing several animations as of writing). Some occasional performance drops and streaming hitches but overall not an issue.

I wish I could do a mixed review.

This game immediately impresses on first impression, with the graphics, the physics (we all had fun drawing on the whiteboard), and the vibe. 

Bringing players back to city17 hits you with that wave of nostalgia, and what an interesting area to explore in VR.

Then after a few hours you realise how much not just the setting, but the developers want to restrict how much  fun you can have with the gameplay.

So to start, all weapons are one-handed, the design and tactility are nice, the feel of them is not.
A one-handed shotgun is never going to feel good, and the designs really pulled me out of the experience, because there is no realistic explanation for why the player would be restricted to one-handed weapons aside from it being a bad choice from the devs.

Then there's enemy variety, which is somehow even worse than HL2, aside from the zombies which are always fun, a majority of what you'll be fighting is..... headcrabs, which now come in a variety.
Aside from the standard, and the speedy variation you now have an armored, and get this, an electric headcrab.
Whoever thought playing whackamole with a blue, bullet sponge, shocky spider boi, chasing him around the room after every shot would be fun, needs to be fired.

And Gabe if it was you stick to Steam, please.

Oh yeah there's also combine but very, very rarely.
You'll fight like 2 at a time and they have even worse AI and are now more static on rails enemies, designed to just shoot at you from behind one cover.

I'm not even going to finish it, considering Valve can't even finish the Half-Life series, and instead wants us to buy a spinoff, why should I?

single_points.text: One reviewer says the native release lagged a lot when barnacles spit and killing two simultaneously was enough to crash the game, while running good on Linux with Proton.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the game consists of small arenas with hallways in between, making fights extremely predictable when encountering obstacles you cannot return from.

citation.review_text:
It took me 6 years to finally finish Half-Life: Alyx. As a VR game, it's utterly brilliant, especially on the Steam Frame. I doubt you'll find a better experience anywhere. As a Half-Life game, it's pretty meh. It'll all small arenas, with hallways in between, sometimes a puzzle. It's extremely predictable where fights are going to happen, the same way you know you're going to fight in Gears of War when you see a lot of places to take cover up ahead. It's always some obstacle that you won't be able to return to (like dropping from a height), and that's when you know you'll fight some enemies. And it just takes a lot of the fun away. I'd kill for a new VR Portal game, that would be amazing.

33/43 achievements.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-game players note the total absence of melee weapons and close-quarters striking options.

claims.claim: Reviewers note the complete absence of melee combat mechanics and the inability to use weapons like a crowbar.

citations.review_text:
There is not much to say. 
The game looks awesome. The feeling hits just right, I am not a big horror guy but the scary parts were just fine. The gameplay is smooth and fair.
Minor minus is that there is no melee at all in the game, in my opinion a miss. VR+Crowbar = ♡.
The story is at times fun and then again quite straight firward and really makes you miss the Valve games from the mid 2000s to 2010s.

EDIT:
I feel like I ended this review overly negative! So I thought I'd bring this up! This is one of the best VR games to ever exist! Its extremely fun! The story is awesome! The horror elements are wonderful! The script is great, the graphics are great, the gunplay is great, pretty much the entire game is fun! So please, if you want to have one of the best VR experiences play this game!

Hi. This game is amazing. It’s beautiful, the combat is fun, and the hands are WONDERFUL!!! The story is also amazing. All of those things make the game worth playing if you have a VR headset, but it certainly has some major issues!



I should mention the one thing that really annoys me. The innovation is disappointing, it came out after all the innovative games, like Bonelab, Boneworks, and Blade and Sorcery, I just loved this games, and they’re cheaper and you can’t get way more time out of them and they have great performance, but the big thing they didn’t add is melee combat. I mean, the crowbar was such a big thing about Half-Life! Not the end of the world, but sad nonetheless.

Let’s talk about the obvious one: the performance sucks. This game was made in 2020 and it can’t run well no matter how hard I try. On my first playthrough, I was forced to upgrade my RAM just to get it working at 40 fps, and it would crash on 50% of the loading screens. I would blame this on my PC (recently I upgraded to an exceptional gaming/AI laptop that should be able to run this at 70 fps, but I’m stuck at 30), but it ran other games (Bonelab, Boneworks, etc.) at a stable 60-70 fps! I mean, for such an old game that’s supposedly “the most well optimized VR game,” I expected better. Again, I would blame this on myself, but it seems like a common issue. Give it a try, but if it has terrible performance, I suggest you refund it! Enjoy exploring City 16!
The game it self was very good, but I have one big problem with it, you see there is no melee combat you just use your pistol to shoot random crabs. Please add melee
